title: Runbook step
description: One instruction someone will actually run. Stage 9 (#34 — promoted from producesCandidate to produces when this schema was built, which is what promoting a candidate means). ⚠️ The type that makes the evidence loop load-bearing: REQ-0009 says no instruction may rest on a claim whose basis is below what that instruction requires, and this is where that is enforced rather than described.

allOf.$comment: #58's destructive floor. Nested inside allOf per #82.

then.$comment: A destructive step with no remediation and no backing claim is the single most dangerous thing this system could emit. The schema refuses it; #57's threshold and #96's verdict are then checked by the lint, which can see the evidence graph.

instruction.description: What to do, stated so it can be executed without interpretation.

expectedOutcome.description: How the operator knows it worked. Without this a step cannot fail, only appear to.

ordinal.description: Position within its runbook. Ordering only — dependencies are trace edges, not numbers.

destructive.description: #58: whether this step can destroy something. Classified per step; the schema requires remediation and a backing claim when true.

remediation.description: What to do if this step fails or must be undone. Required when destructive (#58's floor).

restsOn.description: The assertions this instruction depends on being true. ⚠️ The edge REQ-0009 is about: the lint reads each target's DERIVED verdict and confidence (#96) and blocks a step resting on a claim that is `refuted`, `contested`, or below its required rung. That check cannot live here — JSON Schema cannot see an evidence graph.

partOf.description: The runbook this step belongs to.

dependsOn.description: Steps that must complete first. A real edge rather than an implication of `ordinal`, so reordering cannot silently break a dependency.

x-unresolvableTraceTargets.description: #75: runbook is activated but not yet implemented, so partOf dangles until it is.
